I am Mariana Barreto Alcantara, a first-year student at the University of California, Berkeley, double majoring in Neuroscience and Business Administration. Originally from Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, I have spent the past four years in the United States and am passionate about applying the knowledge and skills I have gained here to strengthen Brazilian public health.

As a Junior Research Intern, I contribute to public health communications aimed at educating communities on healthy living practices and the role of scientific research in promoting well-being. My work also spans social sciences and computational epidemiology, where I help develop systems to visualize public health data and identify the social factors that most significantly influence disease spread across different contexts.

Driven by my roots and my interdisciplinary background, I am committed to bridging scientific research and community impact in Brazil.
